PullRequest.Title: Move Monaco Editor checks to a separate GH action

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The workflow call count, script implementation, moved consumers, and absence of a browser-directory cache are directly visible. Exact download duration varies by runner/network, but the duplicated boundary and its placement before hygiene checks are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Playwright browser archive bytes, extraction CPU, and runner disk I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is one extra installation of Playwright's full default browser set for every matching pull_request and push workflow event; retries can repeat the network operation on failures.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased CI latency and excessive network/disk work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The CI hygiene job installed Playwright once and then ran the Monaco ESM and browser tests that consumed those browsers.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new Monaco workflow installs Playwright for the moved browser tests, but the original CI hygiene job still unconditionally installs the same default browser set even though all Monaco browser consumers were removed from that job.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: `.github/workflows/monaco-editor.yml:56` adds a new unconditional browser installation while the same diff removes every Monaco browser-check step from the old hygiene job but leaves that job's existing `yarn playwright-install` in place, increasing the scenario from one installation to two.
Findings.Title: Remove the duplicate Playwright browser download
Findings.Impact: Every PR and matching push now downloads/extracts the default Playwright browsers twice on separate Ubuntu runners. The second, now-unused installation remains on the hygiene job's critical path, delaying that required result and consuming additional runner/network capacity.
Findings.Evidence: Line 56 invokes `yarn playwright-install`; package.json maps this to `installDefaultBrowsersForNpmInstall()`. The only Playwright consumers in `test/monaco` are the moved `esm-check` and editor tests. After the diff, the remaining hygiene steps are hygiene/layering/build/eslint/TypeScript checks, and repository searches show no Playwright use in those hygiene/layering commands. The cache action stores only `**/node_modules`, not Playwright's browser installation directory.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep line 56 for the Monaco tests, but remove the now-unused `Download Playwright` step from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so each event installs the browser set only in the workflow that consumes it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Monaco Editor checks on each pull request or push to main/release branches
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new workflow must complete checkout, Node setup, node_modules cache restore (or Yarn install on a miss), Playwright browser installation, compilation/bundling, and Chromium/Firefox tests. Before the PR, the same Monaco commands waited behind hygiene/layering/eslint in one job; after the PR they run in a separate parallel workflow, so the extra setup is on Monaco's path but the hygiene commands are no longer on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout the repository on a new runner
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional checkout per matching workflow event
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Monaco checks reused the checkout already performed by the CI hygiene job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before any Monaco check can start

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the `**/node_modules` Actions cache, or fetch dependencies with Yarn on a miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache restore per event; one additional full Yarn dependency installation on a cold/partial cache path
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Monaco checks reused the hygiene job's cache restore/Yarn installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before compilation and tests; exact warm hits skip Yarn

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download and extract Playwright's default browser set
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install in the new workflow plus the unchanged install in CI, for two installs per event; Playwright's browser directory is not covered by the configured node_modules cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A single install in the hygiene job served the Monaco browser checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Necessary for the Monaco Chromium/Firefox consumers in this workflow

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run TypeScript, gulp/webpack, and Monaco browser-test subprocesses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed sequence per event; browser tests run once each for Chromium and Firefox
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands ran later in the CI hygiene job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These are the authoritative checks and dominate the post-setup path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workflow event frequency (every matching PR and push); command cardinality is fixed per event rather than repository-item fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One new Ubuntu runner executes concurrently with the existing CI jobs. Steps inside the Monaco job are sequential, and its test runner executes Chromium then Firefox sequentially. On a cold node_modules cache, it can race the existing Ubuntu jobs for the same cache key; on an exact hit, Yarn is skipped.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The node_modules cache key and restore fallback match existing Ubuntu jobs. Exact warm hits avoid Yarn; misses or partial restores run Yarn. No configured cache covers Playwright's browser installation directory, so that boundary remains unconditional on hosted runners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: workflow triggers, step order, cache conditions, and invoked scripts are directly traceable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner startup, checkout, cache, and browser-download durations vary, but the extra runner boundaries and duplicate browser installation are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: The parallel split can shorten Monaco result latency despite duplicating setup. The separate setup itself is an intentional scheduling tradeoff; the second Playwright install is reportable because the old install now has no consumer.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hygiene, layering, eslint, and declaration checks on each pull request or push
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing hygiene job still performs checkout, Node/cache setup, and an unconditional Playwright browser installation before all remaining hygiene checks. Monaco compilation/bundling/tests were removed from the tail, but the browser download remains before the first hygiene command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download and extract Playwright's default browser set
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One now-unused installation per matching event, concurrent with the necessary install in the Monaco workflow
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The install was needed by the Monaco ESM/browser tests that followed later in the same job; the diff removes all of those consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks every hygiene/layering/eslint/declaration check even though none consumes the browsers

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing suite per event, with work scaling to repository files as before
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same checks ran before the Monaco checks in the same job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authoritative work after setup; unchanged by the diff

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One redundant browser-set installation per workflow event; total waste scales linearly with PR/push frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: This job runs concurrently with the new Monaco workflow, so both invoke Playwright installation at roughly the same time on independent hosted runners. Hygiene's own steps remain serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: node_modules retains the pre-existing exact/fallback cache behavior. The stale Playwright step is unaffected by node_modules cache hits because browser binaries use a separate location not listed in the cache paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all remaining hygiene commands and Playwright references were inspected, and the removed Monaco commands are the only consumers on this job path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser bytes and delay depend on the hosted image and network, but the unconditional duplicate boundary and lack of downstream consumers are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: the move adds the necessary install in the new workflow but fails to remove the now-unused original, doubling browser installation work and delaying hygiene.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced both workflow scenarios, setup/cache paths, subprocesses, browser downloads, and changed concurrency. Submitted one medium-confidence performance finding for the duplicated Playwright browser installation; the other duplicated setup costs are intrinsic to the intentional parallel-job split and are partially bounded by the shared node_modules cache. No regression-fix record was warranted because the PR's parallelization benefit lacks evidence of a specific shipped regression and symptom.
